gap: No result ChatGPT got states price per litre of build volume. Worked out from maker prices on 2026-11-09, the three QIDI printers are both the cheapest per litre and the only candidates with an actively heated chamber that reaches 65 °C: Max4 $20.28/L, Plus5 $22.75/L and Q2 $24.06/L, against $26.76/L for the Bambu P2S (passive chamber), $35.59/L for the Flashforge AD5M Pro (passive) and $81.00/L for the assembled Prusa CORE One+ (55 °C chamber).
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages and the top results. goodprints3d.com (cited) gives no prices, build volumes or chamber temperatures. 3dprinterlab.net (cited) lists build volumes but no prices, and gives a heated-chamber figure only for the X2D (65 °C). speakcad.com/blog/best-3d-printer-for-functional-parts (rank 1) gives launch prices, build volumes and chamber temperatures for older models (Q1 Pro, CORE One, X1C, K2 Plus, H2D) but never divides one by the other. None of them computes dollars per litre or sets ChatGPT's three cards against a QIDI machine at the same price.
decides: This changes ChatGPT's 'best all-around' pick for anyone printing ABS, ASA or nylon. At $449 the QIDI Q2 costs exactly what the P2S costs on sale, but it gives 18.66 L against 16.78 L (11% more) and a 65 °C actively heated chamber against the P2S's passive one. Bambu's 'no actively heated chamber' is quoted from The Crafty Catsman because bambulab.com blocked my fetches. For PLA and PETG parts the P2S is still reasonable. The CORE One+ costs about 3.4× the Q2 per litre and its chamber tops out at a lower 55 °C, so its case rests on repairability, not on value or heat.
